description.value: The study investigated sex differences in gray matter volume and brain-behavior relationships in patients with stimulant dependence after prolonged abstinence.

spans.text:
To investigate whether sex modulates the effects of stimulant dependence on gray
matter volume (GMV) in patients who have achieved long-term abstinence and to
characterize how sex modulates GMV according to specific behavioral measures, such
as dependence symptom count, behavioral approach, and impulsivity.

value: Significant negative correlations were found between the severity of drug use and GMV in the bilateral nucleus accumbens. This correlation was driven by women with stimulant dependence; a steeper and significant negative correlation was seen in women compared with men, in whom the correlations were not significant. The negative relationship between severity of drug use and nucleus accumbens GMV suggests that women may demonstrate greater susceptibility to changes in the severity of drug use.
